Conclusions in brief

  • We simplified the plan because the original needed labels nobody has. It required someone to mark leaf traits on every photo. Instead we use an expert field guide table (Go Botany: which species has which leaf) plus public, species-named photos, so no manual labelling is needed.
  • BioCLIP already names common species well (93% correct first guess on fresh 2026 photos). Our job is therefore not to name, but to give checkable reasons, the way an expert would. iNaturalist does not offer this today.
  • The reasons are getting reliable. Reading the leaf edge improves from 0.80 to 0.86 when we train on more species (47 → 368), and to 0.86 when the model looks at a close-up leaf crop (1.00 = perfect, 0.33 = guessing).
  • Next: make every reason carry an honest confidence, and let the system learn new species with one expert answer per group of look-alike photos.

1 · Pipeline

One line from photo to species, plus a loop that learns new species

Each box is measured separately below.

2 · Data

1,503 clean leaf photos from 3,114 fresh 2026 iNaturalist downloads

No manual labels: species names plus the Go Botany trait table give the labels.

Method

Finding: no dataset labels traits per photo, but species-level trait tables plus species-labelled photos give trait labels for any number of photos.

3 · S0 · How far can leaves go?

Even perfect leaf reading puts the right species in the top 5 only 79% of the time

Fruit and flower traits are needed to separate look-alikes.

Method

Go Botany profiles only, no images; each trait is read correctly with probability p; 20 draws per species.

4 · S1/S2 · Leaf sorter

The leaf sorter keeps the right photos: precision 91%, recall 95%

1,503 of 3,114 photos pass.

Method

Logistic regression on DINOv3 embeddings; threshold chosen on validation; zero-shot text veto tested but not used.

5 · S3 · Image fingerprints

Photos of the same species sit close together: 7 of 8 nearest neighbours match

Each photo becomes a list of numbers; similar plants get similar numbers.

Method

BioCLIP 2.5 ViT-H/14 image embeddings (results/s3_bioclip.npz).

6 · S4 + S7 + S8 · Reading leaf traits

Leaf edge: 0.80 on whole photos, 0.86 with more training species, 0.86 with leaf crops

Traits are learnt without any per-photo labels.

Method

Labels from Go Botany species values (species with one recorded value only); logistic regression on frozen embeddings. S8 adds iNat leaf photos of more Go Botany species to training; the test photos are unchanged.

7 · Same leaf, every model

Same leaf, every model: where the evidence chain holds and where it breaks

Each row is one model reading the same photo; ✓ = agrees with the field guide.

Method

Test photos = iNat 2026 leaf photos of 'described' and 'unknown' species (not used to train trait models). BioCLIP top-3 = zero-shot 'a photo of ' over the 120-species set (BioCLIP 2.5 ViT-H/14 text vectors × results/s3_bioclip.npz). Traits = most probable value from the trait models. Trait matching over the 120-species set with all 10 leaf traits.

8 · S5 · Naming the species

BioCLIP names 93% correctly; leaf traits alone reach 35% top-5

Traits are the evidence behind a name, not a rival namer.

Method

Method: photos uploaded and taken in 2026 (after BioCLIP's training data), leaf photos kept by the S2 sorter; trait models trained on the 'known' species only; BioCLIP zero-shot prompt 'a photo of '. Re-ranking BioCLIP with traits did not change top-1 (93.2% → 92.7%). Crops: Grounding DINO 'a leaf.' boxes (≥ 1 box on 1,269 of 1,454 photos), up to 3 crops per photo. Code: s4_traits.py, s5_match.py, s5_zeroshot.py, s6_evidence.py, s7_crops.py.

9 · S6 · Evidence chain

76% of answers come with supporting leaf evidence; leaf edge causes 59% of conflicts

A conflict is a cue to look again, not a verdict.

Method

Trait weights chosen on other species; 'no evidence' = the read traits do not distinguish the answer from other candidates.

10 · iNaturalist fit

iNaturalist gives a ranked list; we add the reasons

Checkable trait evidence fills a gap the community has asked about.

TopiciNaturalist todayWhat our evidence chain adds
